newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen sliding on troubles, scandals.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen sliding on troubles, scandals.

text.p: South Korea's usual suspects -- corporate financial troubles and scandals -- would combine to keep share prices falling on Monday, traders and brokers said.
The composite price index fell 8.64 points in Saturday's half session to 678.98 after declining much of last week.
Alex Kim, broker at Hanwha Securities, said the market might shed as much as one percent by the end of the day Monday.
"There are not many positives supporting this market," Kim said.
A stronger yen against the dollar is the only positive factor, he said, because that could make Korean exports more competitive in world markets.
Outstanding margin loans, which now top three trillion won, are making investors nervous about a big sell-off, Kim said. Most of such loans come due in June and July, he said.
"Market sentiment is getting bad," said Casey Choe, trader at Union Bank of Switzerland. "We don't have any external market supports. The market will continue to consolidate."
